Meta.title: Marlon Werth: software design, development and AI integration
Meta.description: Marlon Werth designs and builds software from the first sketch to a running system: web and app development, 3D and VR, AI integration, hosting and documentation.

Footer.tagline: Software from the first sketch to a running system.

hero.title: I design and build software, start to finish.
hero.lead: I'm Marlon Werth, a software engineer and researcher at DFKI in Osnabrück. I plan the system with the people who will use it, design the interface, write the code, run it in production and write the documentation. Where AI helps, I build it in.

services.title: From the first sketch to a running system
services.intro: Most of my projects need several disciplines at once. I can take on the whole thing, or join your team for the part where you need a hand.

design.title: Software design
design.body: Requirements, system architecture and process models in BPMN. I work these out with the people who will use the software before anyone writes code, and I have run workshops on process modelling at work and at universities.

build.title: Web and app development
build.body: Full-stack web apps with React, Next.js and Nest.js, mobile apps in Flutter, and the SQL, document, time-series and graph databases behind them.

xr.title: 3D and VR
xr.body: VR applications in Unity for Meta Quest with hand tracking. I model, rig and animate the 3D assets in Blender myself.

ai.title: AI integration
ai.body: Speech recognition, language models and model results built into products and everyday workflows, plus synthetic training data: in Godot I generate labelled thermal camera footage for fall detection models. In my own development I orchestrate AI coding agents across planning, implementation and review, with tests and code review as quality gates.

ops.title: Hosting and operations
ops.body: Docker, Kubernetes on a VPS, GitLab CI/CD, GitHub Actions, Vercel and Nginx on Linux. I host and maintain what I build, so deployment is part of the plan from the start.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.body: Architecture notes, setup guides and handover documents that let someone else pick the project up. When the project is a study, that includes a research paper.

secai.title: SECAI smart heating app
secai.summary: A heating service app from a research project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs (BMWE). It uses AI services to lower energy use and heating costs. I worked on it as part of a team.
points: Built the Nest.js backend: authentication, account management, and the connection between several databases and the client app.
Set up Kubernetes on a virtual private server and containerized every service and database with Docker.
Wrote the GitLab CI/CD pipeline that takes code from the repository to the server and out to the app.
Connected partner devices through Azure IoT Hub, so the backend can read and control them.
secai.imageAlt: Overview screen of the SECAI heating app on an Android phone, showing today's consumption and room temperatures

tandem.title: VR reading tandem
tandem.summary: A VR app that helps children learn to read German. It runs natively on Meta Quest and is controlled by hand tracking.
points: Built in Unity, with 3D assets I made in Blender.
Speech recognition checks how well a child reads each passage. Google Cloud APIs handle translation and text-to-speech.
Designed with the Design Science Research method and tested several times with experts and with children.
The findings are published in a research paper.
tandem.imageAlt: The VR reading tandem menu: an open storybook floating in front of the player's hands

crai.title: Crai platform
crai.summary: A platform where organizations assess their AI use cases against the requirements of the EU AI Act.
points: Proposed the system architecture and shaped the platform with the client around their workflows.
All content lives in Strapi, so the client can extend the platform without code changes.
A custom backend connects the frontend to AI services that automate the assessment.
User management with role-based access keeps each organization's use cases separate.

godot.title: CITAH: synthetic thermal data for fall detection
godot.description: A Godot project that generates synthetic thermal camera clips for training fall detection models. An animated person walks through a 3D room and either falls or keeps walking, and a custom shader pipeline renders the scene as heat values. The output matches the real sensor: two 60×40 cameras joined side by side, 165° field of view, about 25 fps. Each clip ships with labels marking when the fall starts and ends. A Python step finishes the images and compares them against real reference footage, and a small GUI configures scenarios and generates clips in batches.

tandem.title: VR reading tandem
tandem.description: A reading trainer for children set in the forest from Little Red Riding Hood. The children read the story aloud to move it forward, and speech recognition checks their pronunciation.

video.title: Video generator
video.description: A Python tool that writes a short story with Google Gemini, turns it into speech, times captions to the audio, lays everything over a random video template and uploads the result without any manual step.

dashboard.title: AI web dashboard
dashboard.description: A dashboard for an AI model that monitors a smart cowshed. Results arrive over a websocket in real time, next to live camera images, temperature and humidity.

circularity.title: Circularity Navigator
circularity.description: A web app that teaches companies about the circular economy and circular design. They choose design principles for their products and export them.

bpmn.title: BPMN website and app
bpmn.description: A web app for drawing BPMN diagrams, which are stored as graphs in Neo4j. A Flutter app then walks users through the process step by step.
